When a feature/task is:

- implemented
- tested
- reviewed

IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT AUTHENTICATION RULE:

During development, DO NOT change the existing demo users or the mechanism used to switch between roles/permissions.

The existing development/demo role mechanism is intentional and must remain available for testing.

After development is complete, production authentication will be implemented properly and the development/demo mechanism will be removed/replaced as part of the production-security phase.

rules.text:
The tracker MUST NOT interfere with, modify, break, or otherwise affect the EJE application.

The EJE application is:

    VOID-za/EJE-Managment

The tracker MUST be a completely separate project.

Separate:

- Git repository
- directory
- database
- database user
- environment file
- systemd service
- application process
- logs
- configuration
- migrations
- backup strategy
- deployment
- HTTP port
- authentication
- source code

The tracker must NEVER:

- import tracker code into EJE
- modify EJE package.json
- modify EJE tsconfig

rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3B: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER CORRECTION + DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Maintain the security controls already implemented:

- scrypt password hashing
- passwords never committed
- passwords never logged
- passwords entered securely
- hashed sessions
- CSRF protection
- session-bound CSRF
- CSP
- nosniff
- frame protection
- no-referrer
- HSTS
- parameterised SQL
- ORDER BY whitelist
- audit logging
- read-only bearer access
- loopback binding
- hardened systemd service
- read-only EJE checkout mount

Do not weaken these controls.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3B: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER CORRECTION + DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
This is extremely important.

Do not tell us a rule is authoritative merely because it sounds correct.

Do not fabricate historical wording.

Do not reconstruct a supposed rule from general software engineering principles.

Distinguish:

WHAT THE PROJECT OWNER ACTUALLY SAID

from

WHAT THE CODE CURRENTLY DOES

from

WHAT THE PROJECT DOCUMENTATION SAYS

from

WHAT CLAUDE RECOMMENDS

from

WHAT IS INFERRED.

The tracker must preserve those distinctions.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3B: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER CORRECTION + DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026

rules.text:
Perform a cleanup sweep.

Look for:

- dead exports
- unused imports
- duplicate rule records
- duplicate implementations
- obsolete comments
- obsolete documentation
- stale task descriptions
- stale deployment instructions
- stale source references
- abandoned code
- unused files
- unnecessary dependencies
- contradictory documentation

Remove only what is genuinely obsolete.

Do not remove historical records.

Do not remove useful audit history.

Do not remove superseded requirements.
rules.source: EJE project owner instruction — "EJE PROJECT CONTROL SYSTEM — PHASE 3B: AUTHORITATIVE RULE RECOVERY + TRACKER CORRECTION + DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION", 25 September 2026
